content: 1. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of upadacitinib by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely when upadacitinib is coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 2. Vadadustat increases the levels or effects of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Vadadustat may also increase the exposure of BCRP substrates. Monitor for adverse effects associated with BCRP substrates and adjust their doses according to product labeling. 3. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of valbenazine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2E1 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the valbenazine dose to 40 mg once daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 4. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of vamorolone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the starting dose of vamorolone to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day for patients weighing more than 50 kg. 5. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of vardenafil by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 6. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of velpatasvir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of venlafaxine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of verapamil by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of vinblastine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Monitor for hematologic or gastrointestinal adverse effects associated with increased systemic exposure to vinblastine. Consider temporarily withholding antiretroviral therapy in patients who develop significant hematologic or gastrointestinal side effects. If prolonged withholding is necessary, consider initiating a revised regimen that excludes CYP3A or P-gp inhibitors. 10. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of vincristine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Monitor for hematologic or gastrointestinal adverse effects associated with increased systemic exposure to vincristine. Consider temporarily withholding antiretroviral therapy in patients who develop significant hematologic or gastrointestinal side effects. If prolonged withholding is necessary, consider initiating a revised regimen that excludes CYP3A or P-gp inhibitors. 11. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of vinorelbine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Co-administration of voclosporin and tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) or elvitegravir may increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration with nephrotoxic drugs may increase the risk of acute and/or chronic nephrotoxicity. 13. Voriconazole increases the plasma levels of elvitegravir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of voriconazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration of cobicistat with voriconazole is not recommended unless the benefit-risk assessment justifies its use. 15. Elvitegravir decreases the plasma levels or effects of warfarin by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of warfarin through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor INR more frequently when coadministered with inhibitors of CYP3A4, CYP1A2, or CYP2C19, and adjust the warfarin dose as needed. 16. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of zanubrutinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the zanubrutinib dose to 80 mg once daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Interrupt dosing as recommended for adverse reactions. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor, resume the previous zanubrutinib dose. 17. Zinc decreases the plasma levels or effects of elvitegravir by forming ionic complexes in the gastrointestinal tract. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Administer elvitegravir 2 hours before or 6 hours after polyvalent cation-containing products. 18. Acetazolamide increases the plasma levels or effects of cobicistat and elvitegravir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 19. Anastrozole increases the plasma levels or effects of cobicistat and elvitegravir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 20. Elvitegravir increases the plasma levels of buprenorphine by an unknown mechanism. No dose adjustment of buprenorphine/naloxone is required when coadministered with elvitegravir. Patients should be closely monitored for sedation and cognitive effects. 21. Cyclophosphamide increases the plasma levels or effects of cobicistat and elvitegravir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 22. Drospirenone increases the plasma levels or effects of cobicistat and elvitegravir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 23. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of ganaxolone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Changes in ganaxolone exposure when coadministered with CYP3A4 inhibitors are not expected to be clinically significant. 24. Larotrectinib increases the plasma levels or effects of elvitegravir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 25. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of ixazomib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical trials have shown no clinically meaningful changes in ixazomib systemic exposure when coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 26. Elvitegravir decreases the plasma levels of naloxone by an unknown mechanism. No dose adjustment of buprenorphine/naloxone is required when coadministered with elvitegravir. Patients should be closely monitored for sedation and cognitive effects. 27. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of abemaciclib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase plasma levels of abemaciclib and its metabolites, necessitating dose reduction. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, increase the abemaciclib dose after 3-5 half-lives of the inhibitor to the pre-inhibitor dose. 28. Acalabrutinib increases the plasma levels of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of acalabrutinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of acalabrutinib with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If short-term use of a strong CYP3A inhibitor is necessary (e.g., up to 7 days), temporarily interrupt acalabrutinib treatment. 30. Elvitegravir increases the plasma levels or effects of adagrasib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of adagrasib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors until steady-state concentrations are reached (~8 days). If steady state is not reached, concomitant use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors will increase adagrasib concentrations and toxicity risk. 31. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of ado-trastuzumab emtansine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of alfentanil by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 33. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of alfuzosin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the potential for increased alfuzosin concentrations, which can result in serious or life-threatening reactions such as hypotension. 34. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of alpelisib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of alpelisib (a BCRP substrate) with a BCRP inhibitor may increase alpelisib concentrations, raising the risk of toxicities. If unavoidable, closely monitor for increased adverse reactions. 35. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of alprazolam by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 36. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the plasma levels or effects of elvitegravir by forming ionic complexes in the gastrointestinal tract. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Separate elvitegravir dosing from antacids by at least 2 hours. 37. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of amiodarone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clinical monitoring is recommended when coadministered with antiarrhythmics. 38. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of amitriptyline by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor for antidepressant response. 39. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of amlodipine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of amoxapine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor for antidepressant response. 41. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of apalutamide by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Apalutamide decreases the plasma levels or effects of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) by increasing elimination. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, with drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates can result in lower exposure to these medications. Avoid or substitute another drug when possible. Evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect if coadministration is necessary. 42. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of apixaban by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 43. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of aprepitant by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of aripiprazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the aripiprazole dose by 25%, and by approximately 50% if coadministered with both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and a CYP2D6 inhibitor.
